title: Align session ephemerality with scheduler fairness and reduce KV memory churn
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: the serving runtime currently treats session objects and their KV cache entries as long-lived by default. This causes memory churn and uneven preemption behavior when the scheduler rebalances or preempts slots. Spike findings show frequent short-lived sessions (chat turn micro-sessions) allocate KV segments that survive GC windows, leading to tail memory pressure and SLO spikes. Goal: make session lifetime semantics explicit and align KV ephemerality to scheduler fairness so short sessions don't monopolize cache or cause prolonged eviction storms.
background: Observed behavior: when a high-volume interactive workload (typical PLG chat flows) creates thousands of micro-sessions with small token footprints, the current KV allocation path marks segments as semi-persistent. The slot allocator and lease manager often extend sessions to avoid losing context, but this conflicts with preemption fairness goals for bursty tenants. Related incidents: grafana/dashboard/runtime/mem-pressure-2026-02 (tokenized tail spikes). Previous refactors (ENG-26109, ENG-33109) touched the prefetech and slot prewarmer code but did not address session ephemerality policies.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a session 'ephemerality' flag with three modes: ephemeral (evict aggressively), transient (standard TTL), pinned (existing behavior). 2) Propagate ephemerality from the API layer (per-request header or model route config) down to the KV allocator so allocation paths choose slab tiers and GC hints. 3) Adjust scheduler fairness: when deciding preemption candidates, factor ephemerality score so ephemeral sessions are deprioritized for lease extension. 4) Add a short-lived in-memory bloom filter / LRU hint to avoid recreating tiny KV entries for repeated quick-turn requests, reducing allocation churn. 5) Feature-gate rollout behind config runtime flag kvc_ephemerality_v1.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Positive: reduces steady-state memory usage and eviction storms for bursty interactive workloads; improves fairness and tail latency.
- Negative: incorrectly classifying sessions as ephemeral may regress user-facing continuity (chat context lost) unless routes opt-in.
- Risk: added complexity in allocator tiers and scheduler scoring could cause unexpected scheduling edge cases.
- Mitigation: ship behind feature flag, create canary policy, and provide automatic fallback to pinned semantics if error counters increase.
implementation_steps:
1. API: add optional boolean header X-Session-Ephemeral and route config field 'session_ephemerality'. (PR: runtime-api#1289)
2. KV allocator: add ephemerality-aware slab hints and GC timestamp hints. (PR: runtime-kv#1291)
3. Scheduler: modify lease extension policy to include ephemerality weighting and implement safe fallback. (PR: runtime-scheduler#1302)
4. Add bloom/LRU hint structure to reduce repeated tiny allocations. (PR: runtime-cache#1309)
5. Integration tests: slot preemption simulations, memory pressure simulations, and end-to-end chat continuity tests.
6. Canary rollout to dev region 'us-west-2a' behind kvc_ephemerality_v1 flag.
7. Monitor for two weeks; rollback plan documented.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit and integration tests covering allocation paths for ephemeral/transient/pinned sessions.
- End-to-end e2e flow where ephemeral sessions free KV segments within TTL and do not cause eviction storms.
- Priority fairness metric: preemption fairness index improves by >= 12% on synthetic workload.
- Peak memory pressure on micro-session benchmark reduced by >= 25%.
- No more than 1% increase in context-loss customer errors on canary; otherwise rollback.
metrics_and_dashboards:
Primary: runtime.mem.kv_active_bytes_by_ephemerality (Grafana), runtime.scheduler.preemption_fairness_index (custom), runtime.kv.eviction_rate, runtime.request.context_loss_rate.
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abc123/runtime-ephemerality, runbook notes at https://confluence.redwood.company/display/ENG/Session+Ephemerality+Design.
rollback_plan: If canary shows >1% context loss or >10% increase in tail latency (p99 tokens), toggle kvc_ephemerality_v1=false which reverts allocator hints and scheduler weighting. If rollback fails, abort rollout and open incident with on-call infra and sched teams.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator tier selection.
- Fuzz tests for ephemerality header permutations.
- Load test: 100k micro-sessions per minute generator that mimics PLG chat; capture mem footprint and preemption statistics.
- Chaos test: simulate lease-manager flaps to ensure fallback logic prevents mass context loss.
notes: Design reviewed with infra and platform PMs on 2026-02-25. Decision: prefer opt-in ephemerality via route config to avoid accidental regressions for enterprise customers who expect pinned context. Consideration: integrate with Optimize recommendations later to suggest ephemerality for specific endpoints based on workload profile.
